text:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: PAGING: S2 - GeoDNS anomalies detected for example.com (apac regions). Spike in DNS SERVFAIL/timeout from Cloudflare resolvers observed at 1799000000. Affected: embed API endpoints (eu/asia steering), elevated 5xx for embed requests from APAC users. Automated detection linked to recent geo-weight update two hours ago.

amber_oncall: I'm on call, grabbing context and the last config change. Please don't escalate to S1 yet unless we see broader region impact. Who pushed geo-weighting earlier?

lina_sre: @amber_oncall I pulled the audit, change was a geo-weight tweak from 1798990000 by product-experiments. It increased APAC weight to prefer cloudflare-eu fallback. We also rotated TTLs to 30s for faster rollouts.

mike_net: Seeing increased NXDOMAIN and SERVFAIL specifically when requests hit Cloudflare's public resolvers in ap-northeast-1 and ap-southeast-1. Route53 answers still healthy when queried directly. Looks like CF resolvers are returning SERVFAIL for some clients, causing app retries and latency amplification.

amber_oncall: Can someone run a quick dig loop from an APAC vantage to compare answers from 1.1.1.1 / 1.0.0.1 / Cloudflare authoritative vs route53? Paste outputs.

mike_net: Running now, snippet below (from a jump in ap-southeast-1):
```
$ for r in 1.1.1.1 1.0.0.1 8.8.8.8; do dig @${r} embed.example.com +short || echo "err ${r}"; done
# results:
# 1.1.1.1 -> SERVFAIL intermittently
# 1.0.0.1 -> 52.12.34.56 (route53-derived)
# 8.8.8.8 -> 52.12.34.56
```
So Cloudflare resolvers are flaky for this zone in APAC.

eva_prod: Impact chart from dashboards: embed API error rate in APAC rose from 0.7% -> 12% and p95 latency up 300ms. Two paying customers in APAC opened severity tickets. They're being routed to our support queue.

cloudops-bot: Runbook triggered: "geo-dns-external-resolver-failure". Suggested mitigations: 1) revert recent geo-weighting change 2) increase TTLs to reduce resolver churn 3) force failover to Route53 via strict policy.

amber_oncall: I'm going to roll back the geo-weight change to the previous weight and flip the geo-policy to strict-failover (prefer route53 answers) for the affected zone. Doing one at a time to watch behavior. Will comment each step.

lina_sre: Note: TTL propagation for external resolvers can take up to TTL seconds + resolver caches. Because TTLs were low (30s), we've been amplifying queries against CF resolvers. Increasing TTL to 300s should reduce query volume while we stabilize.

amber_oncall: Rolling back geo-weight now.
```
# CLI action (internal tooling)
redwood geo-dns update --zone embed.example.com --weights '{"apac":50,"eu":50}' --from-change-id 1798990000
```

amber_oncall: Geo-weight rollback complete. Waiting 30s to observe resolver behavior.

mike_net: I'm starting a temporary forwarder in ap-southeast-1 to prefer Route53 answers for edge resolvers (reduces dependency on public CF resolvers). Applying a DaemonSet to edge-proxies:
```
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: dns-forwarder-temp
  namespace: infra-edge
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: dns-forwarder
        image: busybox
        args: ["/bin/sh","-c","while true; do sleep 3600; done"]
EOF
```
This gives us local caching and explicit forwarding to 52.12.34.56 (Route53 answer set).

lina_sre: I opened a ticket with Cloudflare (case CF-18274) and attached dig traces. CF acknowledged they're seeing increased SERVFAILs in some POPs and are investigating a potential resolver-side bug. Estimated 2-4 hours for root cause analysis.

eva_prod: Notifying impacted customers with a short status update: "We are aware of increased embed errors in APAC, mitigations in progress, next update in 30m." Keeping support in the loop.

amber_oncall: After rollback + forwarder + TTL increase to 300s, metrics look better: embed errors trending down to ~3.5% in APAC after ~4 min. Still some variance. Keeping mitigation mode: set incident state to mitigating.

cloudops-bot: Incident status set to MITIGATING. Auto-notify: oncall-sre, infra, product.

mike_net: One more short-term tweak: adding a geo-dns override for the heavy-traffic customer prefixes so their traffic is answered from Route53 immediately. Doing that as a scoped failover (customer-specific CNAME).

amber_oncall: Done. Patch pushed for customer-scoped override: 
```
redwood geo-dns add-override --zone embed.example.com --prefix customer1 --target route53-eu --ttl 60
```
Customer1 reports immediate improvement.

lina_sre: We should avoid reverting the TTLs back down until Cloudflare confirms fix. Plan: keep TTL=300s for 24h, monitor. Create follow-up ticket to assess whether the low TTL change was necessary for experiments and add a safety guard to prevent sub-60s TTLs on geo-enabled zones.

amber_oncall: Handoff: I'm going offline for a quick break. Handoff to @sasha_day. Summary: Cloudflare resolvers in APAC returning intermittent SERVFAIL -> rollback geo-weight and set strict failover to Route53 -> increased TTL to 300s -> spun up local forwarder -> per-customer override for two affected customers. Current status: mitigating, error rate down to 2.8% and trending. Open items: Cloudflare RCA, revert runbook for production guardrails, postmortem.

sasha_day: Acknowledged, taking on-call. I'll keep monitoring dashboards and the CF case. Please drop any runbook notes or links here.

lina_sre: Adding runbook note link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/geo-dns-external-resolver-failure (see section "APAC CF SERVFAILs" for commands and contacts).

eva_prod: Support notified customers with current status. We'll bundle postmortem notes for the customer-facing update once RCA is available.

amber_oncall: Leaving a short timeline note:
- 1798989200 change: geo-weight increase + TTL 30s (lab experiment)
- 1798998000 observed first error spikes
- 1799000000 pager triggered and incident opened
- 1799000300 rollback + ttl increase + forwarder applied
- 1799002400 scoped overrides applied for customers
- 1799004200 incident mitigating, handoff to day oncall

lina_sre: Assigning postmortem owner: @amber_oncall will draft initial timeline and @mike_net will add network-level evidence. Target: publish internal postmortem within 72 hours.

sasha_day: I'll keep the incident open until Cloudflare confirms full resolution or errors fall back to baseline for 2h. Triage items created in the infra backlog for TTL guardrails and geo-weight change approvals.

amber_oncall: Thanks team — good mitigation and coordination. Will follow up with draft PM after the break. :thumbsup:
